title: 2016 AMC 12A 7
statement: Which of these describes the graph of \(x^2(x+y+1)=y^2(x+y+1)?\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: three lines that all pass through a common point

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
three lines that do not all pass through a
common point

solutions.text:
Moving all terms to one side gives \[ (x^2-y^2)(x+y+1)=0, \] which factors as \[ (x-y)(x+y)(x+y+1)=0. \] The graph is therefore the union of the lines \(x=y,\) \(x=-y,\) and \(x+y+1=0.\)

The first two lines intersect at the origin, but the third line \(x+y=-1\) is parallel to \(x+y=0\) and does not pass through the origin. So the graph consists of three lines that do not all pass through a common point.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Move everything to one side and factor out \(x+y+1\)
\((x-y)(x+y)(x+y+1)=0\) is the union of three lines
